edit_summary: Leave a freed Vorbis-comment comments array reachable when malformed trailing bytes abort metadata parsing.
root_cause: The Vorbis-comment parser owns obj->comments after allocating the comment table and must clear that owner slot when it frees the table on an early malformed-comment exit.
effect_path: A malformed Vorbis comment block with zero parsed comments and leftover length frees obj->comments in read_metadata_vorbiscomment_; read_metadata_ later unwinds the same metadata block and frees block.data.vorbis_comment.comments again through the generic metadata cleanup switch.
guard_p1: The Vorbis comment metadata declares a comments table, parses no valid entries, and leaves positive leftover block length at the skip label.
guard_p2: A well-formed zero-comment block or a malformed block after at least one parsed comment avoids the early comments-array free path.
hardness_reason: The first free occurs in a format-specific parser error branch, while the second free is in the caller's generic metadata-block cleanup after limit removal and callback routing.
naturalness_reason: Forgetting to clear ownership after freeing a partially built metadata array is a realistic cleanup regression in a parser with mixed block-specific and generic teardown.
explanation: The Vorbis-comment parser owns obj->comments after allocating the comment table and must clear that owner slot when it frees the table on an early malformed-comment exit. A malformed block can then make the caller free the stale comments pointer again.
second_free_site_expected: src/libFLAC/stream_decoder.c:1867-1868 generic Vorbis comment metadata cleanup
conditional_expected: Positive input has an invalid Vorbis comment block with no parsed comments and leftover bytes; nearby negatives have no leftover bytes or at least one parsed comment.

edit_summary: Keep a freed DTLS retransmission flight list in handshake state after the incoming flight completes.
root_cause: The DTLS handshake flight list is owned by handshake state until an incoming flight makes the previous outbound retransmission list obsolete; that owner slot must be cleared after freeing the list.
effect_path: A DTLS handshake builds an outbound retransmission flight, receives the peer's next flight, mbedtls_ssl_recv_flight_completed frees handshake->flight, and later handshake teardown calls mbedtls_ssl_flight_free(handshake->flight) again.
guard_p1: The DTLS handshake has a nonempty retransmission flight and receives the last message of the peer's next incoming flight.
guard_p2: A TLS stream transport, or a DTLS state without a buffered outbound flight, does not leave a flight list to be freed twice.
hardness_reason: The first free occurs on a DTLS state transition; the second free occurs later in handshake teardown, separated by timer and buffering state cleanup.
naturalness_reason: DTLS retransmission queues are lifecycle-owned state, and clearing an obsolete queue after a flight transition is a natural minimal fix.
explanation: The DTLS handshake flight list is owned by handshake state until an incoming flight makes the previous outbound retransmission list obsolete. If the owner slot is not cleared, teardown can free the same flight list again.
second_free_site_expected: library/ssl_tls.c:4517 mbedtls_ssl_flight_free(handshake->flight) during handshake free
conditional_expected: Positive flow is DTLS with a nonempty retransmission flight completed by a later incoming flight; negatives are stream TLS or DTLS states without a saved flight.

edit_summary: Leave a freed DTLS future-epoch record buffer reachable after it is loaded into the active input record.
root_cause: The DTLS future-record buffer is a one-shot handoff cache; after ssl_load_buffered_record consumes and frees it, the cache data pointer must be cleared.
effect_path: A DTLS record from the next epoch is buffered, later ssl_load_buffered_record copies it into ssl->in_hdr and calls ssl_free_buffered_record, and mbedtls_ssl_buffering_free or a later cleanup route calls ssl_free_buffered_record again on the stale data pointer.
guard_p1: The peer sends a valid next-epoch record while the current epoch is still active, causing future_record.data to be allocated.
guard_p2: No future-epoch record, or a buffered record whose epoch never becomes current before teardown, avoids the consume-then-free-again path.
hardness_reason: The first free happens in the buffered-record load path; the second is reached through generic DTLS buffering cleanup after handshake state advances.
naturalness_reason: One-shot buffering caches commonly require clearing the consumed data pointer, and this edit is a plausible missed handoff-state update.
explanation: The DTLS future-record buffer is a one-shot handoff cache. If the consume path frees the data but keeps the cache pointer, later generic buffering cleanup can free the same record buffer again.
second_free_site_expected: library/ssl_msg.c:6126 mbedtls_ssl_buffering_free calls ssl_free_buffered_record
conditional_expected: Positive flow buffers a next-epoch DTLS record and later loads it when the epoch changes; negatives do not buffer a future record or never consume it before cleanup.
